subject: Orbit3B: Burst 503 pattern — recovery commitments & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@skyline.ai
Date: 2025-05-11T09:12:00Z
Subject: [ALERT] orbit3b: 503 burst (09:10 - 09:22 UTC)

Heads-up — monitoring flagged a sustained 503 spike from orbit3b starting ~09:10 UTC across eu-west-1. Key observations:
- 09:10–09:18: error rate rose from ~0.3% to 6.7%
- 09:14–09:20: median latency increased from 85ms to 420ms
- errors correlated with increased KV cache evictions on host pool-a (see short logs attached)

Immediate actions taken:
- throttled non-critical background batching jobs (karthik did this at 09:14)
- enabled degraded-mode fallback to orbit3b-lite for tiered customers (partial routing)
- created incident RW-2345 and added Skyline ops to the ticket

I'll stay with triage and pull logs — tagging Marissa for kernel/runtime review and Karthik for rollout decisions.

Attachments: timeline-gantt.png (quick timeline)

--
Dylan Brooks
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@skyline.ai>, ops@skyline.ai, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-11T09:35:00Z
Subject: Re: [ALERT] orbit3b: 503 burst (09:10 - 09:22 UTC)

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the quick triage.
Jane / Skyline ops: sorry for the disruption. We are prioritizing a mitigation-first approach to keep your traffic healthy while we investigate root cause. Planned immediate steps (next 2 hours):
- enforce stricter request-level circuit breaker (grace->runtime) for large payloads (rolling 09:45)
- expand routing to orbit3b-lite for 20% of traffic (minimizes regressions)
- collect full request traces and KV eviction traces and share logs by 10:30 UTC

Can we hop on a 30-min call at 10:00 UTC to align on cutover tolerance and to review logs as they arrive? Dial-in: +1 415 555 0123 / meet: redwood.com/meet/ops-call.

I've attached the quick timeline we used to coordinate with SRE.

Attachments: timeline-gantt.png

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@skyline.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, ops@redwood.com, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-12T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Orbit3B 503s — initial logs and notes

Hi Grace / team — thanks for the rapid response and for scheduling the call. We pulled logs from our side and uploaded a combined request dump and request-ids list. Observations from Skyline:
- our retries from SDKs increased at 09:13 and again at 09:16 which amplified load on orbit3b
- clients with >64k token context saw higher error percentages
- we saw a small cluster of requests with repeated identical prefixes that may have caused cache churn

We attached a trimmed log bundle (orbitsvc-logs-20250511.zip). We think a short-term request-size limit + suppressing client retries could reduce load quickly while you look at cache policy.

Attachments: orbitsvc-logs-20250511.zip

— Jane Doe
Head of Platform Reliability, Skyline AI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Jane Doe <jane.doe@skyline.ai>
Date: 2025-05-12T14:20:00Z
Subject: RE: Orbit3B 503s — mitigation and temporary config changes

Summary of what engineering validated during triage call:
- root cause (probable): KV prefix-frequency churn on pool-a combined with a kernel tensor allocator path that degrades above 1024 token windows. The chain increases latency which triggers request timeouts and downstream retries.
- immediate mitigations applied at 12:30 UTC: tightened eviction thresholds, limited convolution kernel to lower mem pressure, and applied request-size throttle at the routing layer.
- result: error rate reduced from peak 6.7% to ~0.6% by 13:05 UTC; latency medians fell back under 130ms for the majority of requests.

Next steps we will follow (post-incident):
1) postmortem draft and timeline (in progress) — we will share an editable draft by EOD tomorrow (see attached postmortem-draft.md).
2) short-term fix: kernel allocator patch + routing throttle (scheduled canary 05/13 02:00 UTC).
3) medium-term: KV policy rewrite to prefer hot-prefix pinning + quantized KV caching on pool-a (target: 2 weeks).
4) offer: we will extend a 10% service credit for any SLA-eligible calls impacted during the window; formal credit proposal in separate email.

Marissa available for technical deep-dive if Skyline wants a follow-up session.

--
Marissa Cole
VP Engineering, Inference Runtime, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@skyline.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-13T16:48:00Z
Subject: Orbit3B: recovery confirmation and commitments (incident RW-2345)

Hi Jane — following up with the closure notes and concrete commitments for RW-2345. Thank you and your ops team for the fast collaboration.

Incident summary (short):
- Window: 2025-05-11 09:10:00 UTC — 2025-05-11 13:05:00 UTC
- Impact: elevated 503s and latency for a subset of Skyline traffic routed to orbit3b (peak error rate 6.7%)
- Root cause (preliminary): KV cache churn on pool-a + allocator path regression for >1024 token sequences

Recovery & commitments:
- immediate: mitigations described by Marissa were implemented and stabilized by 13:05 UTC on 05/11
- canary patch: kernel allocator fix scheduled for 05/13 02:00 UTC (canary) and full rollout 05/14 pending verification
- medium-term: KV policy rewrite + quantized KV caching target 2 weeks
- customer remediation: 10% service credit for impacted calls (formal credit note to follow)
- transparency: we will share the postmortem draft and internal timeline in the next 24 hours and incorporate Skyline feedback

Request: please reply to confirm you received these commitments and whether Skyline would like a technical walkthrough of the postmortem (we can schedule a 60-min session with Marissa and the runtime leads).

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md (draft), timeline-gantt.png

Thanks again — we prioritize preventing recurrence and reducing unit impact.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
